page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfr9i.16xlarge is an x86_64 instance belonging to the high clock speed server family, engineered for memory-intensive and high-frequency computational tasks. The virtual machine runs on KVM virtualization and is provisioned with 64 dedicated vCPUs driven by an Intel Xeon 6982P-C processor operating at 3.4 GHz. System memory totals 512 GB, creating a memory-to-core allocation of 8 GB per vCPU. Dedicated GPU hardware is not included with this instance.

The instance does not feature bundled local disk storage, requiring external network block storage for operating system volumes and application data. Network connectivity is supported by a 36 Gbps baseline bandwidth capacity, enabling rapid data transit between clustered nodes and decoupled storage targets. The absence of local solid-state drives means input and output operations rely on remote storage configurations, while dedicated CPU pinning guarantees unshared compute resources.

Given the combination of substantial memory and elevated clock frequencies, ecs.hfr9i.16xlarge offers balanced resource density for compute-bound applications that also depend on low-latency memory access. Typical production use cases include enterprise in-memory databases, large-scale memory caching, electronic design automation, batch data transformation, and concurrent backend transaction processing systems.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfr9i.16xlarge is a high clock speed virtual machine tailored for memory-intensive enterprise tasks requiring rapid per-core processing. Operating on the KVM hypervisor with an x86_64 architecture, this instance is powered by 64 dedicated Intel Xeon 6982P-C vCPUs clocked at 3.4 GHz and includes 512 GB of system RAM, maintaining an 8 GB per vCPU ratio. No integrated local storage or dedicated GPU hardware is bundled, directing all persistence requirements to remote block storage volumes. System communication is supported by a 36 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile, accommodating substantial data flows. Because the server combines an expansive memory footprint with dedicated high-frequency cores, it avoids CPU contention during peak processing periods. The configuration is particularly well suited for in-memory databases, memory-resident analytics, distributed caching tiers, and high-load transactional enterprise backends.
